artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S$ be a semigroup. A binary relation $\sim$ on $S$ is called a semigroup conjugacy relation if it is an equivalence relation that, in the case $S$ is a group, reduces to ordinary group conjugacy, and that satisfies the standard structural axioms expected of a conjugacy notion on semigroups (in particular it agrees with group conjugacy on every subgroup of $S$).

Define the following two relations on $S$:

(1) Group-style conjugacy $\sim_g$: $a \sim_g b$ iff $a$ and $b$ lie in a common subgroup $H \le S$ and are conjugate in $H$ in the usual group-theoretic sense.

(2) Unit conjugacy $\sim_u$: $a \sim_u b$ iff there exists a unit $u \in S$ (i.e., an invertible element of the monoid generated by $S$, or more precisely an element of the group of units when $S$ is a monoid) such that $u^{-1} a u = b$ and $u b u^{-1} = a$.

One always has $\sim_g \subseteq \sim_u$.

Question: Is $\sim_u$ the smallest semigroup conjugacy relation strictly larger than $\sim_g$? Equivalently, must every semigroup conjugacy relation $\sim$ on $S$ with $\sim \ne \sim_g$ satisfy $\sim_u \subseteq \sim$?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is resolved in the negative within the source itself: a theorem establishes a strict chain $\sim_g \subsetneq \sim_u \cap H \subsetneq \sim_n \cap H \subsetneq \sim_{p^*} \cap H \subsetneq \sim_{tr} \cap H \subsetneq \sim_o \cap H$, showing that other conjugacy relations lie strictly between $\sim_g$ and $\sim_u$ (when intersected with $H$), so $\sim_u$ is not the smallest conjugacy properly above $\sim_g$.

status_evidence.title: Conjugacy relations in semigroups
status_evidence.snippet: So another natural question is whether ∼u is the smallest conjugacy that does not equal ∼g. We now prove that it is not.
status_evidence.claim: The authors explicitly answer the question in the negative.
